note: Comments Order has no configure route (configure=null), no permissions, no Drush, and no plugins. Its entire persistent state is up to three third-party settings on a comment-type field's field.field.* config: comments_order.order (ASC|DESC), comments_order.children_natural_order (1|0), comments_order.created_order (1|0). The extra fields appear on field_config_edit_form only when the field type is 'comment'. At display time comments_order_query_comment_filter_alter() rewrites the comment_filter query ORDER BY, and a CommentsOrderStorage handler keeps pager ordinals consistent. All medium/hard cases are grounded in that real third-party-setting config on namespaced comment fields (field_co_*) on node.article.

evals.prompt: On a Drupal 11 site with the comments_order module enabled, how do I make comments on Article nodes display newest-first instead of oldest-first? There is no settings page for the module — where do I set it and where is that choice stored?
evals.expected_output: There is no configure route. Edit the comment field on the bundle's Manage fields page and set 'Comments order' to 'Newest first (descending order)'. It is stored as a third-party setting on that field: field.field.node.article.<comment_field> -> third_party_settings.comments_order.order: DESC.

evals.prompt: What are the three per-field settings that the comments_order module adds to a comment field, and what does each control?
evals.expected_output: order (ASC/DESC — oldest vs newest first); children_natural_order (1/0 — with DESC+threaded, keep reply chains chronological vs reverse them too); created_order (1/0 — for flat lists, sort by the 'Authored On' created timestamp instead of comment id). Stored under third_party_settings.comments_order on the field.

evals.prompt: With comments_order set to newest-first on a threaded comment field, what does the 'Natural order for children' option do, and which stored key controls it?
evals.expected_output: children_natural_order = 1 reverses only the top-level (parent) threads while keeping each reply chain in natural chronological order; children_natural_order = 0 reverses the children too. It only applies with DESC order on a threaded display.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a comment field named field_co_known on the Article content type, configured with comments_order. Inspect the live field configuration and state which direction (oldest-first or newest-first) its comments are ordered.
evals.expected_output: field_co_known is set to newest-first: field.field.node.article.field_co_known third_party_settings.comments_order.order is DESC.

evals.prompt: On this site the Article content type has a comment field field_co_created configured with comments_order. Inspect its live configuration: is it ordering comments by the comment id or by the 'Authored On' (created) timestamp? Name the third-party setting that decides this.
evals.expected_output: It orders by the 'Authored On' created timestamp because third_party_settings.comments_order.created_order is 1 on field.field.node.article.field_co_created (order is DESC).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the Article content type has a comment field field_co_task whose comments currently display oldest-first. Using the comments_order module, configure this field so its comments display newest-first, and apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set the comments_order.order third-party setting on field.field.node.article.field_co_task to DESC (e.g. FieldConfig::loadByName('node','article','field_co_task')->setThirdPartySetting('comments_order','order','DESC')->save(), or tick 'Newest first' on the field edit form).

evals.prompt: The Article content type on this site has a threaded comment field field_co_thread already set to newest-first, but replies within a thread still read in natural (chronological) order. Using comments_order, configure the field so the child replies are reversed as well (disable 'Natural order for children'), keeping the newest-first ordering. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: On field.field.node.article.field_co_thread keep third_party_settings.comments_order.order = DESC and set comments_order.children_natural_order = 0 (turn off 'Natural order for children'), then save.
